summary: Plant-neutral lifecycle definitions; carob doses and age/site recommendations on carob communities; LIFE schedules remain with LIFE methods. Reassociated 10 carob findings and 6 LIFE project findings without changing their source wording or immutable dose evidence.

topics.label: Nursery watering
topics.description: Watering before field planting prepares nursery plants for the next stage. The regime depends on the plant, growing conditions and nursery stage; this phase does not prescribe a dose or frequency.

aspects.Purpose: Water plants while they are in the nursery, before field planting.
aspects.Amount: No universal dose. Record the selected amount in L/plant/event for the particular plant and site.
aspects.Frequency or trigger: Set the interval or moisture trigger for the species, growing medium, stock and conditions. No universal interval is defined.
aspects.Applicable period: Before field planting; calendar months depend on the growing programme and location.
aspects.Age and stock: Record the nursery or propagation stage. Nursery age is different from time since field planting.
aspects.Limitations: This is a plant-neutral phase definition. Species/community recommendations, project schedules and case observations belong to their own context. Unknown is not zero; seasonal totals and reservoir capacities are not event doses.

topics.label: Settlement watering
topics.description: The first watering immediately after field planting is a purpose category that can be used for any plant. Subsequent establishment watering belongs to maintenance or support according to its purpose.

aspects.Purpose: The first water application immediately after field planting.
aspects.Amount: No universal dose. Record the selected amount in L/plant/event for the particular plant and site.
aspects.Frequency or trigger: At planting. Classify later applications by their purpose rather than calling the whole establishment period settlement.
aspects.Applicable period: At the planting date; no universal calendar month.
aspects.Age and stock: Newly field-planted stock can already be of different ages. This phase is defined by the planting event, not a fixed biological age.
aspects.Limitations: This is a plant-neutral phase definition. Species/community recommendations, project schedules and case observations belong to their own context. Unknown is not zero; seasonal totals and reservoir capacities are not event doses.

topics.label: Summer maintenance watering
topics.description: Recurring watering during summer or another difficult period follows a chosen interval or trigger. Its dose, season and duration must be selected for the plant, site and method.

source_refs.locator: Irrigation purposes and context-dependent regimes; no universal plant dose
Irrigation purposes and context-dependent regimes; no universal plant dose

aspects.Purpose: Recurring water during a period when the chosen planting needs maintenance irrigation.
aspects.Amount: No universal dose. Record the selected amount in L/plant/event for the particular plant and site.
aspects.Frequency or trigger: Record the chosen interval or trigger separately from the amount. The appropriate interval depends on plant and site conditions.
aspects.Applicable period: The locally relevant difficult or dry period; no universal months or season length.
aspects.Age and stock: Record time since field planting and the relevant development stage. There is no universal age-based dose or stopping age.
aspects.Limitations: This is a plant-neutral phase definition. Species/community recommendations, project schedules and case observations belong to their own context. Unknown is not zero; seasonal totals and reservoir capacities are not event doses.

topics.label: Support watering during stress
topics.description: Additional water may be considered in response to unusual weather, soil moisture or plant stress. Support can overlap establishment and maintenance; it is not a final age stage.

source_refs.locator: Irrigation purposes and context-dependent regimes; no universal plant dose
Irrigation purposes and context-dependent regimes; no universal plant dose

aspects.Purpose: Respond to stress or exceptional conditions, rather than follow an assumed standard schedule.
aspects.Amount: No universal dose. Record the selected amount in L/plant/event for the particular plant and site.
aspects.Frequency or trigger: Monitor forecasts, soil moisture and plant condition. Consider support water when the relevant conditions justify it.
aspects.Applicable period: When the relevant stress conditions occur; no universal month or recurrence.
aspects.Age and stock: Can overlap field establishment and maintenance. Assess the particular plant and site instead of using age alone.
aspects.Limitations: This is a plant-neutral phase definition. Species/community recommendations, project schedules and case observations belong to their own context. Unknown is not zero; seasonal totals and reservoir capacities are not event doses.

aspects.Irrigation applicability: These recommendations and observations concern carob trees in the cited setting, not every companion species or every Mediterranean site. Finca practices are examples, not universal doses.
aspects.Nursery watering — carob: The handbook describes frequent growth-stage watering and spaced, more intense hardening irrigation, adapted to the nursery. It gives no universal litres-per-plant dose. Nursery programmes for one- and two-season stock are not years since field planting. See the nursery finding and PDF 72–74, 79.
aspects.Settlement watering — carob: The reviewed carob passages do not supply a single numerical first-watering dose. Do not substitute the LIFE NIEBLAS project’s quantities as a carob recommendation.
aspects.Maintenance watering — carob guidance: The handbook describes a 3–5-year establishment period and advises 1–5 summer waterings during the first five years, without specifying an event dose or an explicit annual count (PDF 95–96).
aspects.Maintenance watering — finca observation: Huerta Los Tamayos: 50–80 L/plant/event, three summer waterings during the first two years (PDF 103). Buenavista: 100 L/plant/event every 15 days during the first two summers, in an intensive production planting (PDF 123). Los Lirios: 50 L/plant/event three times weekly, April–October, in an intensive mother-plant plot; its older afforestation received no establishment irrigation (PDF 112). These settings must not be treated as interchangeable.
aspects.Support watering — carob example: El Triguero reports 50 L/plant/event monthly as emergency watering (PDF 117). Calendar months and the duration of that regime are not specified. This is a finca observation, not a general emergency dose.
aspects.Quantities and age: Keep L/plant/event, frequency, period and field-establishment age separate. Annual area allocations are not event doses. The reported age windows do not establish a universal stopping age.
aspects.Restoration and production models: MR1 restores degraded areas; MR2 uses runoff harvesting (oasificación). MP1 enriches dehesas, MP2 improves afforestation, MP3 establishes extensive production and MP4 is intensive production. Their inputs and objectives differ.
aspects.Regional example: See Carob communities in Almería for Las Labores, La Alcantarilla and La Tórtola. Do not transfer the wider finca doses automatically to arid Almería.

topics.label: Carob communities in Almería
topics.description: Regional examples of carob-associated vegetation in arid and semiarid Almería. Mastic and wild olive are observed at La Alcantarilla and La Tórtola; wider MR2 companions and potential habitats have different evidence. Las Labores is a managed restoration planting replacing almond and olive. These are explanatory regional groupings, not a single formal association. Carob watering evidence is given here by lifecycle phase, with regional/site-specific limits; no dose is inferred for the accompanying plants.

aspects.Nursery watering — regional evidence: No Almería nursery dose is documented in these case accounts. The wider carob nursery guidance is available on Mediterranean carob associations; it is not a locally measured regime.
aspects.Settlement watering — regional evidence: No numerical immediate post-planting dose is specified for these Almería cases. Nursery plant size and planting-hole dimensions do not determine a water dose.
aspects.Maintenance watering — Las Labores: Deficit drip irrigation from May to September, totalling 400 L/plant over that period (PDF 127). Event count, frequency and L/plant/event dose are not specified. Preserve this as a seasonal total; do not divide by an assumed schedule.
aspects.Support watering — MR2: The arid/semiarid MR2 model mentions small establishment waterings and support watering, with runoff capture and favourable microsites, but supplies no numerical dose (PDF 132, 134).
aspects.La Alcantarilla and La Tórtola: The accounts describe little cultural care/naturalized vegetation, but do not quantify an irrigation regime. Do not interpret unspecified amounts as zero (PDF 135–137).
aspects.Age and source limitations: The regional passages do not establish an age-based watering curve or stopping age. Las Labores’ grafting/production chronology remains unresolved. Its documented watering total does not establish a treatment for every carob in Almería.
aspects.Broader guidance: The Mediterranean carob node holds carob-wide nursery and establishment guidance and the non-Almería finca examples, with their individual conditions.

browse_groups.label: Irrigation lifecycle
browse_groups.maintenance_rule: Organize existing records by their recorded subject. Preserve source contexts and identities; membership is not factual evidence. Community planning values remain separate from source knowledge.
browse_groups.description:
The irrigation lifecycle describes why water is applied. It is a framework for any plant, not a watering prescription for a particular species.

1. Nursery: watering before field planting.
2. Settlement: the first water application immediately after planting.
3. Summer maintenance: recurring watering during a difficult period.
4. Support: additional watering prompted by weather, soil moisture or plant stress. Support can overlap establishment and maintenance; it is not a final age stage.

Amounts and timing: L/plant/event means litres per plant for one watering application. Record the amount, frequency or trigger, applicable period and age/stock context separately. Nursery age differs from time since field planting. Do not infer an automatic dose or stopping age from either.

Choose a regime in its own context: soil, rainfall, species, plant size, nursery stock, planting method and water availability affect the decision. Source recommendations, project schedules and case observations have different meanings. A phase label does not supply a universal amount or calendar.

Compare like quantities: a dose per event is different from a batch quantity, seasonal total, annual area allocation or reservoir capacity. Convert only when the denominator and event count are known; preserve the original wording and calculation. Unknown is different from zero, and ranges remain ranges.

Read contextual recommendations on the relevant species or community, and project schedules on the corresponding project or method. Those examples retain their source, location, plant age, season and limitations; they do not become rules for every plant using this phase. Existing working-plan values are independent decisions.

Glossary: IND/IFWC means individual fog water collector. AFDS means Autonomous Fluid Discharge System: a tank level triggers discharge through an irrigation network. The source label SAD is not expanded in its passage; its correspondence with AFDS is an explicit interpretation of the matching operation. A reservoir fill is separate from the water applied directly at settlement.

Select a phase for its purpose, unit, timing and monitoring considerations. Follow the context links to plant/community recommendations or project methods for specific regimes.
